title: Ananias and Sapphira (Acts 5:1–11)
hookLine: a hard story about pretending to give more than they gave
tomorrow: the council wants them dead. one teacher stands up. what does he say?

lines: PART OF THE PRICE, KEPT BACK.
cards: A filter can make a plate of food look bigger than it is. Ananias and his wife Sapphira sell land, like Barnabas did, and bring money to the apostles' feet.
But they keep back part of the price and let it look like everything. Why does their story end so hard? Not because they kept some.
Because they pretended. A gentle heads-up, for anyone listening with kids: this is a hard story, and two people die in it.

teach.b: Watch the hands first. The same gesture as yesterday: money laid at the apostles' feet. Same hands, same feet, same move.
One is a gift; the other is a performance. Peter sees through it: "Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land?"
Then two questions that change how the whole story reads: "Whiles it remained, was it not thine own? and after it was sold, was it not in thine own power?" The land was theirs. The money was theirs.
Keeping some was never the problem.

teach.h: NOT UNTO MEN, BUT UNTO GOD.
teach.b: "Thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God." And "Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost." Some hours later Sapphira comes in, not knowing.
Peter gives her a chance to tell it straight: "Tell me whether ye sold the land for so much? And she said, Yea, for so much."
Then a sound: footsteps. The young men who buried her husband are at the door, and she falls too. Acts ends the scene with "great fear came upon all the church."
Readers take this story different ways: as God's judgment, as a warning to a young community held together by trust, as a sign of how seriously Acts takes honesty. Acts doesn't explain itself.
One to tell a friend tonight: in this story, keeping money was allowed.

how: Christians read this passage in different ways; some read it alongside Acts 4:32–37, the story of Barnabas, as a picture of honest and dishonest giving side by side.

games.why: Ananias' gift was real; the pretending wasn't. Peter says the money was his to keep. what matters is saying what it is.

practice: Rest your hands on your knees, palms up and empty. Let them be the plain truth about what you give, your time, your money, your effort, no more and no less than it is. Breathe with open hands and nothing hidden in them.

wordCard.voice: Ananias and Sapphira. A couple who kept back part of the price and pretended it was all: Acts' hard story about honesty.

orig.note: Greek: to lie. in Acts 5:3 Peter asks why Ananias would lie to the Holy Ghost.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: no pretending; give what you give, and call it what it is. Day nine of Acts.
